sources.citation: M. S. Gazzaniga, J. E. Bogen, R. W. Sperry (1962). Some functional effects of sectioning the cerebral commissures in man*. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sources.notes: Gazzaniga, Bogen & Sperry (1962 PNAS) foundational clinical report on human corpus callosotomy Patient W.J., demonstrating lateralized visual-motor disconnection across divided hemispheres.

sources.citation: M. S. Gazzaniga (2000). Cerebral specialization and interhemispheric communication: Does the corpus callosum enable the human condition? Brain.
sources.notes: Gazzaniga (2000 Brain) 40-year synthesis of split-brain studies (including Patient P.S.'s snow-shovel/chicken-claw test and left-hemisphere interpreter confabulations).

sources.citation: Alex J. Clark, Malte S. Kaller, Jorge Galino, Hugh J. Willison et al. (2017). Co-cultures with stem cell-derived human sensory neurons reveal regulators of peripheral myelination. Brain.
sources.notes: Pinto et al. (2017 Brain) reassessment showing split-brain patients retain unified cross-field motor response selection while visual perceptual comparison stays divided.
